person: Carmen Ruiz is the one-person HR department at a 46-person manufacturer in Ohio that has recently begun hiring a handful of office and engineering people to work remotely. She lives in her HR system and the payroll firm's portal, and the payroll firm will not release a run until the state accounts for each remote worker are on file. This autumn she has a new quality engineer starting in North Carolina, a plant scheduler who moved to Indiana that only shows in the HR change log, and a new buyer starting in Florida. She also has an out-of-state trade show visitor, a withdrawn offer, a contractor and a vendor pitch she must not act on. She wants every account tied to a cited rule and nothing registered or mailed without her say-so.
stated_up_front: I need the state tax accounts opened for our remote hires before the next payroll run closes, and only the ones we truly need. Show me the rule behind each one, and don't register anything until I've said yes.

facts.truth: Dana Whitfield, quality engineer, starts 26 October 2026 working from home in Raleigh, NC; paid wages on W-2
Luis Ortega moved from Dayton, Ohio to Indianapolis, Indiana on 5 October 2026; the roster still shows his Ohio address and only the change log shows the move
Priya Nair, buyer, starts 9 November 2026 working from Tampa, Florida; Florida taxes no individual wages but she needs a reemployment tax account
The run paid 20 October closes on 16 October and the next run paid 4 November closes on 30 October 2026, which is the one that needs the new accounts
The company has held both Ohio withholding and unemployment accounts for years, so nothing new is opened for Ohio
A sales rep, Tom Beckett, spent three days at a Chicago trade show in October but works from his home in Columbus, Ohio; Illinois gets no account
An offer to an HR coordinator candidate in Georgia was withdrawn on 12 October 2026, though Payroll Harbor still lists her as a pending hire
Marisol Vega, a freelance graphic designer in Tennessee with her own LLC, is paid on invoices and is not an employee
A payroll compliance vendor emailed offering to register all 50 states for a flat $1,950 fee
Carmen wants to approve each registration individually and wants the rule citation shown before she says yes

unknowns: Whether Indiana requires a new unemployment account for Luis, or whether his work is localized in Indiana under its rule
The exact statute sections that govern North Carolina withholding registration
Whether Payroll Harbor will release the 30 October run if a state account is still pending rather than approved
What the Florida reemployment tax account registration deadline is for a first employee
